topics.topic: Bootstrap CLI input channel, terminal requirement, and echo behavior
questions: From which channel must the command read the email, password, and confirmation, and must it refuse redirected or non-terminal standard input?
From which concrete channel must the command read them, must it require an interactive terminal, may redirected standard input be used, and which inputs must have terminal echo disabled?

quotes: run_bootstrap_cli: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the email from the terminal at execution time, read the password twice without echo, refuse a mismatch before it constructs the store, and resolve the database location through the existing runtime settings boundary.

run_bootstrap_cli: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST accept the password only from the interactive no-echo prompt, never from a process argument, an environment variable or a configuration file, and MUST NOT echo, print, or log that password or its hash on any path, including the message it prints when the store is already initialized.
judgement.why: The later notes require terminal input and an interactive no-echo password prompt, thereby excluding redirected password input and specifying that both password entries have echo disabled.

topics.topic: Bootstrap confirmation value, comparison, and mismatch handling
questions: What is being confirmed, what value must it match, and how is the comparison performed?
What value is confirmed, how is equality tested, and does a mismatch immediately produce exit code 1 or permit another attempt?

quotes: run_bootstrap_cli: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the email from the terminal at execution time, read the password twice without echo, refuse a mismatch before it constructs the store, and resolve the database location through the existing runtime settings boundary. It MUST return the exit code the bootstrap command outcome table assigns to the outcome it reached: 0 for an account created, 1 for a confirmation that did not match, 2 for rejected identity input, 3 for a bootstrap already completed, and MUST report each of those outcomes distinctly in what it prints: describing a completed bootstrap as invalid input tells the operator to correct an address that was never the problem.
judgement.why: The later note identifies confirmation as the second password entry and requires a mismatch to be refused with exit code 1 before store construction, rather than prompting again.

topics.topic: Bootstrap operational-failure behavior, output, and exit codes
questions: What must the CLI do, and which exit code must it return, when the transaction, password hashing, account insert, audit insert, input read, or output write fails operationally?
What exit code and observable output apply when input acquisition, password hashing, database access, transaction commit, or audit insertion fails?

quotes:
Each refusal is its exit code. A configuration or storage failure is none of
the four outcomes: the operation raises it and returns no exit code, and the
failure status the host process then ends with is outside the closed
contract of A29.
judgement.why: The later public-operation contract says operational failures propagate without a command exit code and explicitly leaves the host process's resulting failure status outside A29's closed outcome contract.

topics.topic: Bootstrap refusal-check precedence and winning exit code
questions: When more than one refusal condition applies, which condition and exit code win?
In what order are completion, identity validation, and confirmation checked, and which exit code wins when several refusal conditions apply?

quotes: run_bootstrap_cli: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the email from the terminal at execution time, read the password twice without echo, refuse a mismatch before it constructs the store, and resolve the database location through the existing runtime settings boundary.

bootstrap_first_administrator: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST normalize the supplied email and validate the supplied password through the existing staff identity input boundary, hash that password exactly as supplied with hash_password of the credential boundary, build the account with StaffRole.ADMINISTRATOR, StaffStatus.ACTIVE, a set email_verified_at and created_by None, and its audit record with ActorKind.SYSTEM and no actor_id, key_version or project_id, AuditAction.STAFF_CREATE, AuditEntityKind.STAFF_ACCOUNT, AuditResult.SUCCESS and no reason_code, and hand both to the port in one call. It MUST NOT open a transaction, query persistence, or perform an authorization check, because no authorized administrator can exist yet.

bootstrap_first_administrator: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise BootstrapAlreadyCompletedError, and never the input rejection, when the port reports an already initialized store, so a repeat attempt changes nothing and the caller can tell a second run apart from a mistyped address. IdentityInputRejected stays reserved for the supplied email and password. A genuine storage failure MUST propagate unchanged and MUST NOT be turned into either refusal. BootstrapAlreadyCompletedError is this module's own exception, defined here at top level as a plain Exception subclass whose body is pass and raised without arguments; it is not imported.
judgement.why: The later notes order confirmation before store construction, identity validation before the port call, and the already-initialized decision after the port reports it, so mismatch wins first, then input rejection, then exit code 3.

topics.topic: Caller authorization required to invoke bootstrap
questions: Does the command enforce a caller identity or privilege requirement, rely solely on operating-system executable/database permissions, or permit any local caller who can launch it and reach the database?

quotes: bootstrap_first_administrator: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST normalize the supplied email and validate the supplied password through the existing staff identity input boundary, hash that password exactly as supplied with hash_password of the credential boundary, build the account with StaffRole.ADMINISTRATOR, StaffStatus.ACTIVE, a set email_verified_at and created_by None, and its audit record with ActorKind.SYSTEM and no actor_id, key_version or project_id, AuditAction.STAFF_CREATE, AuditEntityKind.STAFF_ACCOUNT, AuditResult.SUCCESS and no reason_code, and hand both to the port in one call. It MUST NOT open a transaction, query persistence, or perform an authorization check, because no authorized administrator can exist yet.

run_bootstrap_cli: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST be the only entrypoint that reaches the bootstrap operation bootstrap_first_administrator; no http route, router registration, or generated api document may expose it.
judgement.why: The later notes explicitly forbid an application authorization check and restrict access structurally to the local CLI, leaving caller control to the host's ability to execute that entrypoint and reach its configured storage.
